title: Credit Transactions: The Debtors Journal
summary: Selling on credit, debtors and the risk of bad debts, the invoice as source document, recording credit sales in the Debtors Journal, receiving payment from debtors, and posting to the ledger.

notes.text: Many businesses allow trusted customers to buy goods now and pay later. This is a **credit sale**. A customer who owes the business money is a **debtor**. Debtors are an **asset**, because the business expects to receive the money.

rows: Attracts more customers and increases sales
Some debtors may never pay (**bad debts**)
The business waits for its money, which can cause cash-flow problems
Competes with other shops that offer credit
Extra administration: statements, reminders, collecting payments

notes.label: Remember
notes.text: Before allowing credit, a business should check the customer's **creditworthiness** (ability and willingness to pay), set a **credit limit** and agree on **payment terms**, e.g. 30 days.

When goods are sold on credit, the business issues an **invoice** (the original goes to the customer and the business keeps a **duplicate**). The invoice shows the invoice number, date, customer's name, a description of the goods, quantity, price and total amount owed.

notes.caption: Debtors Journal of Kasi Fashions, March 2025 (mark-up 50% on cost)

notes.text: No money is received when goods are sold on credit, so there is **no Bank column**.

notes.title: Sales and cost of sales
notes.problem: Goods are sold on credit for R1 200. The business adds 50% on cost. What goes in the Sales and Cost of sales columns?
steps: Selling price is cost + 50%, so it is 150% of cost.
Sales column: R1 200. Cost of sales column: R800.
notes.answer: Sales R1 200 and Cost of sales R800, giving a gross profit of R400.

notes.text: Each invoice is also posted to the individual debtor's account in the **Debtors Ledger** (a subsidiary ledger), so the business knows how much each person owes. The total of all individual debtors' balances must equal the balance of the **Debtors control** account in the General Ledger.
When a debtor pays, a **receipt** is issued and the payment is recorded in the **CRJ**: in the Bank column and in the **Debtors control** column. It is NOT recorded as sales again.

notes.title: A debtor's balance
notes.problem: L. Mokoena owed R0 on 1 March. She bought goods on credit for R1 500 (4 March) and R900 (22 March), and paid R1 000 on 28 March. What does she owe on 31 March?

questions.prompt: Give TWO advantages and TWO disadvantages of selling on credit.
questions.memo:
Advantages (1 each): more customers/sales; loyalty; competitiveness
Disadvantages (1 each): bad debts; cash-flow problems; extra administration

questions.prompt: Give TWO things a business should do before allowing a customer to buy on credit.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): check creditworthiness/credit history; check income/employment; set a credit limit; agree on payment terms; get references
